title: Sequences
summary: A sequence is an ordered list $a_1,a_2,\ldots$; it converges if $\lim_{n\to\infty}a_n=L$ exists. Limit laws, the squeeze theorem, and monotone-plus-bounded arguments determine convergence — the groundwork for infinite series.

sequence.plain: An ordered list of numbers indexed by $n$.
sequence.in_class: Written $\{a_n\}$; a function on the positive integers.

converges.plain: The terms approach a finite limit.

monotone convergence.in_class: A key existence theorem for limits.

recursive sequence.plain: Each term defined from previous ones.

squeeze for sequences.plain: Trap $a_n$ between two sequences with equal limits.

concept_sections.heading: Limits of sequences
concept_sections.explanation: A sequence converges to $L$ if its terms get and stay arbitrarily close to $L$. Compute limits with the same tools as functions: divide by the highest power, use known limits.
math_steps: Take $\lim_{n\to\infty}$ using algebra or known limits.

concept_sections.heading: The squeeze theorem
concept_sections.explanation: If $b_n\le a_n\le c_n$ and $b_n,c_n\to L$, then $a_n\to L$. Handy for terms with bounded oscillating factors like $\dfrac{\sin n}{n}$.
math_steps: Show both bounds share a limit.

concept_sections.heading: Monotone and bounded
concept_sections.explanation: A sequence that is monotonic and bounded must converge (even if you can't find the limit). This proves existence for recursive sequences.

concept_sections.heading: Divergence
concept_sections.explanation: Sequences diverge by growing without bound, or by oscillating (like $(-1)^n$) so no single limit exists. Recognizing divergence prevents wasted series tests later.

real_world_examples.title: Repeated averaging
real_world_examples.scenario: Newton's method refines a guess each step.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: The iterates form a recursive sequence converging to the root.

real_world_examples.title: Drug half-life leftovers
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: The remaining amount is a geometric sequence $a_n=a_0 r^n\to0$.

real_world_examples.title: Digital sampling
real_world_examples.scenario: A signal sampled ever more finely.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: The sample values form a sequence whose limit is the true value.
